title: VCI Profile
description: Design document 9.3. Whereas the registration definition (7.1) states 'where the library is', this declares 'how to handle that VCI'. Whether this can be expressed as data decides whether the framework approach succeeds. Installed on the device outside this software, not distributed as an extension package (9.3, ADR-228).

match.description: Which VCI this applies to. Matched against discovery results

abi.description: Overrides the values inferred in 7.1.2. If inference is wrong on ARM, fix it here (no core change needed)

symbolDecoration.description: Support for the Windows x86 _Name@N format

concurrentOpen.description: 8.8.1. Whether multiple devices can be open simultaneously. If false, a separate worker is used per VCI

buttonEvents.description: 10.4. Whether triggers can be read from buttons on the VCI unit itself (non-standard, vendor-specific)

readsBatteryVoltage.description: Whether it can be used for the precondition checks in 8.9.1

comparamMapping.description: 8.5. Mapping from COMPARAM to J2534 PassThruConnect flags / PassThruIoctl

quirks.description: Known quirks. Any quirk that cannot be expressed declaratively requires a core change (P4)

initSequence.description: Sequence of calls required after open

postCallDelays.description: Wait time required after specific API calls

fallback.description: Fallback. If none, the feature is disabled

reopenAfterError.description: Reopen the device on receiving these error codes

threadAffinity.description: Many J2534 DLLs are not thread-safe (3.4)

minMonitorPeriodMillis.description: 10.3. Measured values are authoritative; this is only a rough upper-bound guide

machineModeSupported.description: Whether it runs in machine mode (as a service). false for libraries that require an interactive session

signatureVerifier.description: 11.3. Also shown in the Web UI

firmwareUpdate.description: 8.9.1. Updating the VCI itself is left to the vendor's official tool; this system only verifies
